issue.body:
Clarify HJ-2 identity and melanterite phase evidence in Peng et al. (2023)

Source: Peng, R., Shen, J., Li, S. and Liu, H., “Sediment-isolated Comamonas terrigena strain HJ-2: a novel nitrate-dependent ferrous-oxidizing bacterium with multifunction on pollutant transformation,” DOI https://doi.org/10.1093/lambio/ovac022.

The complete publisher HTML, all five original main figures and official supporting DOCX (Methodology S1, Figures S1–S3, Tables S1–S8) are available and inspected. This is a source-clarification follow-up, not a missing-access claim or an assertion that the maintained qualified record is defective.

1. The main identification paragraph assigns HJ-2 to C. terrigena and reports 100% 16S similarity to NBRC 14951, accession AB680720.1. Supporting Figure S1 and current AB680720.1 instead identify that comparator as C. testosteroni. The article's own HJ-2 accession MZ701937.1 currently identifies C. thiooxydans strain HJ-2. Reconcile the experimental isolate, sequence, species assignment and claimed CCTCC AB 2021274 deposit using traceable original sequence/culture metadata. Do not silently rename the experimental strain based on one conflicting label.

2. Supporting Figure S2 assigns melanterite (PDF 01-0255) at 13.35% among mixed phases. The paper does not provide a phase-quantification method, uncertainty/standard, solid collection time, washing/drying/oxygen exposure, or comparator-solid XRD. Obtain the original diffraction data and preparation/quantification details, and clarify whether matched uninoculated/no-nitrate solids were characterized. This is needed to distinguish culture-associated phase assignment from residual FeSO4 crystallization during preparation. A separate Fe(II) sulfate assignment does not itself prove incorporation into a ferric mineral lattice.

Acceptance: retain the narrow source-assigned culture-associated phase observation until the identity and phase evidence are reconciled. Any stronger microbial-causality or phase-yield claim requires actual comparator/preparation and quantitative evidence. The 144 h solution endpoint must not be assumed to be the XRD harvest time. No isolated iron recovery is currently demonstrated.

Evidence: research/sources/round95-sulfates/20261015T124816Z-source-investigation.{json,md}; originals and current GenBank records under /private/tmp/cmm-round95-sulfates-research. Exact-name/DOI search of /private/tmp/cmm-round95-initial-issues.json returned no match; coordinator should repeat live all-state dedup before posting. No author contact has been made.
